extracted.intended_audience: GAP users and package developers (people writing GAP code and extending the GAP library)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference-manual guidance and API specifications for using and implementing GAP functions, dictionaries, hash tables, records, and collection utilities. Includes behavioral contracts for functions and recommendations for package authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: EvalString and local variables
rubrics_metrics.description: If EvalString is used inside a function, then it doesn’t know about the local variables and the arguments of the function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workaround: define global variables in advance and assign the values of local variables to those globals before calling EvalString (example provided). See also ReadAsFunction (10.3.2) and Section 10.3 for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: CrcString behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: CrcString(str) computes a CRC (cyclic redundancy check) number from a string str and returns an integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also CrcFile and HexSHA256 for related checksums. Example: CrcString("GAP example string"); returns an integer (example shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: HexSHA256 behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: HexSHA256(string) or HexSHA256(stream) returns the SHA-256 cryptographic checksum of the bytes in the string or of the data in the input stream read from the current position until EOF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checksum is returned as a string with 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits. Examples given for string and InputTextString("abcd").

rubrics_metrics.name: Pluralize semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Pluralize([count,] string[, plural]) returns an attempt at the appropriate pluralization of a string (considered as a singular English noun).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments: optional non-negative integer count, non-empty string (singular), optional plural form. If plural is given it is used; otherwise an informed guess is made. If count omitted returns plural form; if count n != 1 returns "\>n\< plural"; if count == 1 returns "\>1\< string". Use StripLineBreakCharacters to remove the control markers \< and \> from the return value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calendar functions use Gregorian calendar
rubrics_metrics.description: All calendar functions use the Gregorian calendar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of limitations: operations may not make sense for early dates (before 1582 or before Gregorian adoption in specific countries). See DayDMY remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: DaysInYear contract
rubrics_metrics.description: DaysInYear(year) returns the number of days in the year year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: DaysInYear(1998) -> 365.

rubrics_metrics.name: DaysInMonth contract
rubrics_metrics.description: DaysInMonth(month, year) returns the number of days in month number month of year and fails if month is not in the valid range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: DaysInMonth(3,1998) -> 31.

rubrics_metrics.name: DMYDay behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: DMYDay(day) converts a number of days, starting 1-Jan-1970, to a list [day, month, year] in Gregorian calendar counting.

rubrics_metrics.name: DayDMY behavior and validity
rubrics_metrics.description: DayDMY(dmy) returns the number of days from 01-Jan-1970 to the day given by dmy (a list [day,month,year]); returns fail for input outside valid ranges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note about early dates: results may not be meaningful before Gregorian adoption in various countries (see text).

rubrics_metrics.name: WeekDay contract
rubrics_metrics.description: WeekDay(date) returns the weekday of a day given by date, which can be a number of days since 1-Jan-1970 or a list [day, month, year].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: WeekDay([11,3,1998]) -> "Wed".

rubrics_metrics.name: StringDate behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: StringDate(date) converts date to a readable string. date can be a number of days since 1-Jan-1970 or a list [day,month,year].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: StringDate([11,3,1998]) -> "11-Mar-1998".

rubrics_metrics.name: HMSMSec contract
rubrics_metrics.description: HMSMSec(msec) converts a number msec of milliseconds into a list [hour, min, sec, milli].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: HMSMSec(Factorial(10)) -> [1,0,28,800].

rubrics_metrics.name: SecHMSM contract
rubrics_metrics.description: SecHMSM(hmsm) is the reverse of HMSMSec: converts [hour,min,sec,milli] to milliseconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided in manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: StringTime behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: StringTime(time) converts time (given as number of milliseconds or a list [hour,min,sec,milli]) to a readable string.

rubrics_metrics.name: SecondsDMYhms contract
rubrics_metrics.description: SecondsDMYhms(DMYhms) returns the number of seconds from 01-Jan-1970, 00:00:00, to the time given by DMYhms (a list [day,month,year,hour,minute,second]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Gregorian-calendar remarks for DayDMY apply; last three arguments must lie in appropriate ranges. Example: SecondsDMYhms([9,9,2001,1,46,40]) -> 1000000000.

rubrics_metrics.name: DMYhmsSeconds inverse
rubrics_metrics.description: DMYhmsSeconds(secs) is the inverse function to SecondsDMYhms: converts seconds to [day,month,year,hour,minute,second].

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX representation recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: For generating LaTeX source code with GAP it is recommended to add new functions which will print the LaTeX source or return LaTeX strings for further processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: no clear notion of default LaTeX code for non-trivial mathematical objects; different output may be required in different contexts; containing LaTeX generation in a single function gives a clean overview. Alternative approaches via default methods are possible but less suitable. Package authors are encouraged to add an index entry 'LaTeX' to the documentation of all LaTeX string producing functions so that ?LaTeX lists them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing dictionary type and parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating a dictionary (NewDictionary(obj, look[, objcoll])) the user must choose whether it is only used to check whether objects are known or to store associated information (lookup dictionary), and indicate which kind of objects are to be stored (sample object obj).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If objcoll (a domain/collection containing all objects to be used) is given, performance may improve and obj may be false. NewDictionary attempts to find a suitable internal storage for fast operations. If look is true dictionary will be a lookup dictionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to supply objcoll to NewDictionary
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing objcoll (the domain/collection) to NewDictionary helps choose a more efficient dictionary implementation (e.g., enables hashing vs. sorted lists).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: for vectors, giving the vector space allows hashing; for permutations, providing Elements(SymmetricGroup(n)) can enable position/indexing storage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use RepresentationsOfObject to inspect dictionary representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a dictionary has been created, RepresentationsOfObject can be used to check which representation (internal storage) is used by GAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the manual show different representations returned depending on parameters (IsListDictionary, IsPositionDictionary, IsSortDictionary, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: DictionaryByPosition behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: DictionaryByPosition(list, lookup) creates a new (lookup) dictionary which uses PositionCanonical in list for indexing. The dictionary has an entry dict!.blist which is a bit list corresponding to list indicating the known values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If look is true, dictionary will be a lookup dictionary, otherwise ordinary.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsDictionary vs IsLookupDictionary
rubrics_metrics.description: IsDictionary(obj) tests whether obj is a dictionary (growable collection with ability to add objects and check known-ness). IsLookupDictionary(obj) is true for dictionaries that permit retrieval of associated values using LookupDictionary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are category predicates used to describe objects and choose methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: AddDictionary contract
rubrics_metrics.description: AddDictionary(dict, key[, val]) adds key to the dictionary dict, storing associated value val if dict is a lookup dictionary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If key is not an object of the kind for which the dictionary was specified, or if key is already known to dict, the results are unpredictable.

rubrics_metrics.name: KnowsDictionary contract
rubrics_metrics.description: KnowsDictionary(dict, key) checks whether key is known to the dictionary dict and returns true or false accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: key must be an object of the kind for which the dictionary was specified; otherwise results are unpredictable.

rubrics_metrics.name: LookupDictionary contract
rubrics_metrics.description: LookupDictionary(dict, key) looks up key in the lookup dictionary dict and returns the associated value. If key is not known to the dictionary, fail is returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only on lookup dictionaries; behavior undefined for mismatched key types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hash tables intended primarily for implementers
rubrics_metrics.description: General hash tables described are intended mainly for extending the implementation; programs requiring hash functionality should use the dictionary interface instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hash tables hash by keys and store a value. Keys cannot be removed from the table, but corresponding values can be changed. Fast access to last hash index allows efficient storage of multiple arrays of values but should be used with care.

rubrics_metrics.name: DenseIntKey requirement and guarantee
rubrics_metrics.description: DenseIntKey(objcoll, obj) returns a function usable as a hash key function for objects in objcoll. The function returned is guaranteed to give different values for different objects (one-to-one). If no suitable hash key function predefined, fail is returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If domain not available it can be given as false; DenseIntKey should ideally be implemented efficiently in the core.

rubrics_metrics.name: SparseIntKey behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: SparseIntKey(objcoll, obj) returns a hash key function which may return the same key value for different objects (collisions allowed). If no suitable function predefined, fail is returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when collisions acceptable or domain sparse; SparseHashTable uses result of SparseIntKey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dense hash tables purpose and constructor
rubrics_metrics.description: Dense hash tables are used for hashing dense sets without collisions (in particular integers). Keys stored unordered and values as array with holes; position given by DenseIntKey and KeyIntDense must be one-to-one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DenseHashTable() is the only correct way to construct such a table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sparse hash tables behavior and constructors
rubrics_metrics.description: Sparse hash tables are used for hashing sparse sets: keys stored as array with fail denoting empty positions, values as array with holes, using SparseIntKey results; DefaultHashLength is default starting length; table is doubled when half full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct via SparseHashTable([intkeyfun[, startlength]]). Mapping from integer hash key to index is by taking modulo of the hash array length. DoubleHashArraySize(hash) doubles size and rehashes entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hash key design principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The crucial step of hashing is to transform key objects into integers such that equal objects produce the same integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different types require different functions; GAP provides key functions for some common objects; Dense vs Sparse choice depends on collision tolerance and density.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records: syntax and basic semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: A record is a collection of components each with a unique name (identifier) and a value. Record literals are written rec( ... ) with component assignments name := value. The empty record is rec().
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records usually contain heterogeneous element types; Display can be used to illustrate hierarchy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing record elements (r.name vs r.(name))
rubrics_metrics.description: r.name evaluates to the value of component name in record r; the name is taken literal (not evaluated). r.(name) evaluates second operand name (must evaluate to a string or integer) and then accesses component whose name equals that string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use r.(name) to programmatically access components by name strings or integers; examples provided copying components between records via RecNames.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record assignment semantics (r.name := obj and r.(name) := obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: r.name := obj assigns obj to component name of record r, extending the record if the component doesn't exist. r.(name) := obj evaluates name (string/integer) then assigns to that component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment changes the record object in-place. Use IsBound to test if a component exists and Unbind to remove it.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsBound and Unbind for record components
rubrics_metrics.description: IsBound(r.name) returns true if record r has component name; Unbind(r.name) deletes the component name from the record. Both expect r to evaluate to a record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IsBound and Unbind do not evaluate their argument (special behavior) to allow testing/removal without signaling errors when component absent. Unbind on nonexisting component is not an error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigning components in RecNames order for efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: It is most efficient to assign components to a (new or old) record in the order given by RecNames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RecNames returns a duplicate-free list of component-name strings sorted by RNamObj order which is consistent within a session but may vary across sessions; use Set to obtain session-independent ordering if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record identity and copying semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Two records are identical if changing one by a record assignment also changes the other (i.e., they are two names for the same record object). Record literals create new records not identical to others. Assignment var := r makes var a name for the same record (identical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passing/returning records preserves identity; StructuralCopy and ShallowCopy create new records equal but not identical; ShallowCopy preserves identity of corresponding components whereas StructuralCopy makes components only equal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record comparison/equality rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Two records are equal if for each component of one record the other has a component with the same name and an equal value, and vice versa. Ordering < and <= compares records by imagining components sorted by name and performing lexicographic comparison with unbound elements considered smaller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate equality and ordering; ordering depends on session-specific component-name ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: RNam / NameRNam mapping and session dependence
rubrics_metrics.description: NameRNam(nr) returns the string component name for RNam nr; RNamObj(str) returns the number (RNam) for string str. RNams are assigned dynamically on a first-come, first-serve basis and thus may differ across GAP sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is possible to pass a positive integer to RNamObj where the decimal expansion is used as a string; be aware of session-dependent mappings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record access operations for arbitrary objects (. operations)
rubrics_metrics.description: \.(obj, rnam), IsBound\.(obj, rnam), \.:=(obj, rnam, val), Unbind\.(obj, rnam) are operations called for record accesses to arbitrary objects and allow objects to simulate record behavior if methods installed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For records these operations implement component access, boundness tests, assignment and removal keyed by numeric RNam which must be a positive integer (IsPosInt). Examples show method lookup and invocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsCollection and collections-family utilities
rubrics_metrics.description: IsCollection(obj) tests whether an object is a collection. CollectionsFamily(Fam) returns the family of all collections over Fam. IsCollectionFamily checks whether Fam is a families-of-collections object. ElementsFamily returns the underlying family of elements for a collections family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CategoryCollections(filter) returns the collections category for a filter; DeclareCategoryCollections(name) binds the collections category to a derived name. These utilities are used to manage categories and families when creating collection-related categories (e.g., permutations collections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerator semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerator(listorcoll) returns an immutable list enum. If argument is a list (may contain holes) enum has same length and elements; if argument is a collection that is not a list, enum contains the different elements of the collection in an unspecified order and Length(enum) is the number of different elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: enum[pos] may not be constant-time; size of enum in memory is kept as small as feasible. Default method for lists is Immutable; for non-list collections no default method.

rubrics_metrics.name: EnumeratorSorted semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: EnumeratorSorted(listorcoll) returns an immutable list of the different elements of the argument in sorted order. The argument must be a collection or list whose elements lie in the same family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Length(enum) equals number of different elements; enum[pos] may not be constant-time; memory size minimized. Example use: EnumeratorSorted([1,3,,2]) -> [1,2,3].
